You'll need all the help you can get to stop this endless wall of fuzz from raging! This kill-all circuit explodes the meanest, nastiest, most insane distortion to make you the ruler of the fuzz universe. Details If love is a battlefield, then the Fuzz War is your ticket to victorious sustaining fuzz tone. When there’s nothing between you and the audience except an amp, the Fuzz War, and your axe, crank the Fuzz control all the way up and blow 'em away with the raunchiest fuzz tone in modern history. Or dial back the Fuzz for kinder, gentler overdrives and boosts but without volume limits! The Fuzz War’s specially designed active multi-curve Tone control lets you set your sights on creating glorious music by changing the timbre from a deep sludge-bass rumble to screamin’ top-end lead tones that slice through the mix with a whole bunch of useful sounds in-between. Note: When the Fuzz is turned all the way down, the Tone control acts as a frequency shifter – try it for parked-wah and sick filtered effects! And it wouldn’t be a Death By Audio fuzz pedal without enough output to make even the highest headroom amp beg for reinforcements, which is why there’s a handy Volume control to adjust the output level. Each Death By Audio Fuzz War has sick spray-painted graphix covering up meaty components and sound, giving you a high-tech fuzz mutilator that sounds as good as it looks. Achieve a multitude of ultimate fuzz, boost, overdrive, and distortion sounds with the simple turn of a dial. Listen for yourself and you will see, this is the thickest sounding sustaining fuzz pedal we have ever heard. Controls VOLUME Controls the output volume of the effect. FUZZ Controls the gain of the fuzz circuit. At its lowest setting the pedal just acts as a tone shifter. As the fuzz knob is turned up it sweeps from a booster to an overdrive to a thick distortion to a full on blown out war of fuzz. TONE A specially designed multi-curve shaping filter which changes the timbre of the pedal from super deep bass sludge to screaming highs. Specifications Power Details Power Supply: Standard 9 V

It is not a polite fuzz. It does not “add harmonic content.” It arrives like weather. And for the last decade and a half, an unreasonable proportion of that sound has come out of a big, hand-spray-painted steel box built in New York City by a man who also fronts one of the loudest bands in the five boroughs. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO The Death By Audio Fuzz War is not a subtle pedal, and it has never pretended otherwise. Death By Audio’s own copy for it opens with the line “Call in the Army, the Navy, Scotland Yard, your mom, and the Mario Brothers!” — which tells you roughly everything about the company’s relationship with restraint. But underneath the graffiti and the shouting there is a genuinely well-considered circuit, one specific and unusual control that no other fuzz on the market has in quite this form, and a lineage that runs back through a very particular and very British corner of late-’60s fuzz history. This is not a review. This is a feature on what the Fuzz War actually is, where it came from, who is genuinely documented using one, what it does inside a signal chain, and how to make it behave. How to Get the Tone ↓ Death By Audio: The Warehouse, The Venue, The Workshop Death By Audio was founded in 2002 by Oliver Ackermann, singer and guitarist of A Place To Bury Strangers — a band whose entire live reputation is built on volume, strobe lights and the constant threat of equipment failure as an artistic choice. Ackermann trained at the Rhode Island School of Design, and the company started life not as a pedal brand at all but as a web-based effects customisation service : you told Ackermann what impossible noise you wanted, and he built the circuit to make it. The company’s early years were, in its own words, spent “warehouse-jumping from Virginia to Brooklyn.” What followed was the part everyone in the New York underground remembers: nine years in the Williamsburg building that was simultaneously a pedal factory, a venue, a recording studio and a live-work space, all under the Death By Audio name.
